title: Supreme Court refuses urgent hearing of plea against Ramayana film: 'make your own movie'
dek: The bench declined to list a challenge to the film's censor certificate as the epic nears Rs 1,000 crore net in India, tracker estimates show.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Friday refused to give an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the censor board's certification of Ramayana: Part One, with one judge telling the petitioner that anyone who disagrees with the film's version of the epic should make a film of their own.

The petition, filed by Manoj Singh Thakur and registered on 23 November, challenges the Central Board of Film Certification's clearance of the film and names its producers, Prime Focus Studios and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, its director, Nitesh Tiwari, and its writers, according to reports. His counsel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that several facts in the film were distorted. The Chief Justice noted that the film had already been released and that people who wanted to see it had already done so.

"They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand," Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, according to reports. "Don't waste time of the court." The court did not hear the plea on its merits.

The film, which opened on 5 November and was given a "U" certificate for its Hindi version, is close to Rs 1,000 crore in net takings in India. One box-office tracker estimated its domestic net collection at about Rs 992 crore after 22 days and its worldwide gross at about Rs 1,777 crore. The makers have not published official figures, and trackers' estimates differ.
